title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries, prepared statements, or ORM frameworks. Ensure proper input validation with allow-lists.

title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key, which it uses for authentication, inbound communication, or encryption.
mitigation: Store credentials outside the source tree in environment variables or a dedicated Secrets Management Service.

title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
mitigation: Use context-aware output encoding, Content Security Policy (CSP), and modern frameworks with automatic escaping.

title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
description: The product constructs an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component.
mitigation: Avoid executing OS commands directly. Use library functions or strict allow-list argument validation.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
description: The application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid.
mitigation: Avoid using native language serialization formats (pickle, Java serialization, yaml.load). Use safe JSON or protocol buffers.

title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements such as '..' sequences.
mitigation: Use strict path canonicalization and verify the resolved path stays within the intended root directory.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.
mitigation: Validate and sanitize all user-supplied destination URLs. Restrict network connectivity to private IP ranges and metadata IPs.

title: Improper Authentication
description: When an actor claims to have a given identity, the product does not prove or insufficiently proves that the claim is correct.
mitigation: Implement multi-factor authentication, secure session management, and robust password policies.
